en: The Dharma for Turning the Wheel of the Dharma and Subduing Mara’s Enemies,
translated by the Tripitaka Śramaṇa of Daxingshan Monastery,
the Great Widespread Wisdom Amoghavajra, by Imperial Decree.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mārapramardana addressed the Buddha,
saying: "World-Honored One,
each of the bodhisattvas has already spoken their respective secret mantra teachings."
“Bhagavān, I now wish to speak, for the sake of the future period of the final dharma,
a secret, most excellent, and supremely secret among secrets method for crushing demonic enemies, in order to protect kings and all sentient beings within the realm.”
"I only pray that the World-Honored One will, out of compassion, grant me leave to speak.
The Buddha said, "Speak then.
"World-Honored One, suppose there were a neighboring kingdom that disturbed and invaded our borders."
Either the military forces within one's own country are few and small,
or they are timid and weak,
or there may be subjects who rise up as evil rebels.
One should immediately take the wood of the *nimba* tree and fashion a banner-pole.
It should be twelve finger-breadths in length and eight finger-breadths in circumference, shaved until it is perfectly round,
just as the World-Honored One has commanded.
May all the devas, nāgas, and the eight classes of beings protect all nations, protect all kings,
and protect all sentient beings within the realms of the land.
To eliminate calamities and bring about peace and happiness,
whenever such difficulties arise,
one should depict those deities who protect the nation upon banners.
Those who thus protect the land of the Great Tang are the yakṣas Viśvakarman and Kapphiṇa.
The yakṣa Dharmapāla,
the yakṣa Viśālamukha,
and the yakṣa Viśālaprekṣin.
The yakṣa Rakṣa, the yakṣa Maṇibhadra,
and the yakṣa Pūrṇabhadra.
The Vidyādhara Yakṣa and the Aṭavaka Yakṣa— these and the ten great yakṣas above,
as well as the Vāsuki Nāga King and the Sumanas Nāga King.
The great nāga kings Pūrṇabhadra and Vemacitrin— these three great nāga kings— and the great heavenly queen Hārītī,
the great heavenly queen Airāvaṇā,
and the great heavenly queen Viśālākṣī— these three great heavenly queens— each have five thousand divine generals as their retinue.
All those who are to be depicted should be drawn in their original forms,
holding their respective insignia and painted upon the banner.
Furthermore, at the top of the banner, one should inscribe the ten-syllable *dhāraṇī* of the Unobstructed King (*Anāvaraṇarāja*) Buddha-Usnīṣa.
Finally, the syllable *ṭha* is located in the navel of the wheel.
One should write the names of all enemies,
rebels, and commanders within the spokes of the wheel.
On the base of the banner, draw a wheel complete with eight spokes;
as described above, place the syllable ṬHA in the hub of the wheel.
When a disaster or calamity arises,
one should invite a person who understands the Dharma and has previously received instruction in this teaching.
In the middle of that night, one should construct a square mandala.
Upon that square mandala, one should further draw a triangular mandala.
Then, one should set up this banner in the center of the mandala.
On the four sides of the maṇḍala, place various kinds of food and drink, as well as two *arghas*.
Burn *guggulu* incense and light ghee lamps.
The practitioner who performs the rite of liberation should sit facing south.
Then, one should form the hook seal (ākarṣaṇamudrā) of all Tathāgatas: interlace the fingers of both hands with the palms facing inward to form fists, and extend the right index finger as a hook.
While reciting the mantra, call out the name [of the deity].
Invoke the sixteen great protectors along with their retinues, the deities of great majesty and power, and offer them within the maṇḍala.
The Tathāgata’s hook mantra (*ākarṣaṇa-mantra*) is as follows:
*Namaḥ samantabuddhānām aḥ svadhātala-pratīhata-tathāgata-ghaṭa-kūśa-vṛtti-ja-cakra-pavarga-ha*. Next, the practitioner shall enter the samādhi of the Supreme Vajra Wrathful One of the Three Times.
Visualize [the deity] of blazing majesty and power, with four faces and eight arms;
the left feet trample upon the goddess Umā,
and the right foot tramples upon the god Maheśvara.
Then, one binds the supreme seal of the three times: with the two hands in vajra-fists,
the thumbs and middle fingers hook each other,
and the index and ring fingers are extended straight upward.
Once completed, recite the mantra three, five, or seven times.
The mantra is as follows:

Oṃ suṃbha ni suṃbha hūṃ phaṭ | kīlaya kīlaya hūṃ phaṭ | kīlaya kīlaya pada ya hūṃ phaṭ | ānaya hūṃ va ghaṃ va jra hūṃ phaṭ || Next, perform the *Urdhvadiśā-devatā-ājñā-mudrā* (the seal for commanding the deities of the upper direction): form vajra-fists with both hands.
The two index fingers are interlaced;
having formed the mudrā, one issues this command:
"O you sixteen great protectors, the great yakṣa generals!"
Having received the Buddha’s entrustment,
they shall protect kings and all sentient beings within the realm,
causing them to attain peace and happiness and warding off all calamities and misfortunes.
"Now there is a certain peril within the borders of my kingdom.
You great protectors must assist my military forces to crush the enemy.
You must cause those troops to be bound and rendered bewildered."
"May such-and-such be brought to chaos;
may my army be made powerful and victorious.
Having issued this command, one recites the mantra three times, saying: [the following invocation of the various devas is identical to this, and one forms the fundamental mudrā].
HŪṂ BHAḤ VAJRĪTANADO VAJRAKAŚA HAṂ JAḤ. Furthermore, one should then form the seal for commanding the deities who roam through space: bind the two hands in the vajra-bond.
Bend the two middle fingers so that their nails face each other,
and extend the two ring fingers side by side to press against the two index fingers.
Once the mudrā has been formed:
First, instruct according to the preceding text.
Having given the command,
recite the mantra three times, saying:
Oṃ vajragarbhāya vajra hūṃ. Next, one should form the seal for commanding the deities who dwell in space, which is like the Trailokyavijaya seal.
The two hands encircle one another;
having thus formed the mudrā by placing it upon the crown of the head,
one issues the command according to the preceding text.
Then, recite the mantra three times, saying:
Oṃ vajramara kṣa vaṃ. Next, one should form the seal for commanding the deities dwelling upon the earth: with both hands, perform the vajra-bind.
Extend the two wind-fingers so that their tips meet;
this is the seal of the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi.
Having formed the seal:
First, following the previous text, he issues the command, reciting the mantra three times:
Oṃ vajramantraham. Next, he forms the *bhūmipati-devatā-ājñā-mudrā*: with both hands, extend them so that the palms face outward.
The two heads of the space elements are joined together;
the two wind elements hook together;
and the two fire elements support one another with their heads.
Place the mudrā between the eyebrows.
Following the previous text,
give the instruction and recite the mantra three times as follows:
Oṃ hulu-kaca-vajra-samaya-saṃvanu-stambha-samaya-mūdra-prahaṃ ja-kaca hūṃ phaṭ. Having thus addressed [the deity], [he spoke].
Then, forming the wisdom-hand into a vajra-fist,
press it upon the banner and recite the mantra of the Ten-Syllable Uṣṇīṣa one hundred and eight times.
Regarding the recitation of this Ten-Syllable Uṣṇīṣa mantra:
First, one should form the mudrā and recite [the mantra] seven times. For the mudrā: interlace the two hands with the palms facing inward to form fists;
insert the two thumbs (space-fingers) into the palms;
then bend each of the two index fingers (wind-fingers) so that they rest against the backs of the two thumbs. This is it.
Recite the mantra:
Oṃ vajrasattva śodhaya hūṃ phaṭ. Having completed the recitation, once again burn incense and present flowers.
He then held up the argha offering and made vast,
supreme vows for the benefit, peace, and happiness of the sovereign and all the common people.
Then, forming the vajra-bind mudrā and joining the two fire-fingers (tarjanīs) upright,
it is accomplished.
Recite the Vajra-mukti mantra three times.
Dismiss the assembly of holy beings, each returning to their own palace. The mantra is:
Oṃ vajra muḥ. The ritual proceedings are hereby concluded.
Then, collect the banner and place it within a clean casket or box for storage.
As for the offerings of food, drink, and so forth,
send them away according to the ritual into a river.
The timing for dispatching the army according to lunar mansions, days, and planets;
composed by the Śramaṇa Jingyan of Yanming in Henan, forty-eight [stanzas].
